ar_main_wall.blurb: The main cliff on the north shore of Lake Lincoln, a long sandstone band that runs east to west and faces south. Sport lines make up most of the climbing, with a handful of trad routes and some boulder problems at its base. Grades spread from the 5.7 range up through 5.12, with the densest cluster around 5.10 and 5.11, so there is something for most leaders. Parts of the wall sit in shade while other stretches catch sun. Lincoln it Up, Arachnophobia and Differential Equations are among the favorites, and the easy walk from the lot makes it a popular spot for a short day.
ar_main_wall.parking_note: Use the lot beside the boat ramp on the north side of the lake.
ar_main_wall.approach: Walk past the boat ramp; the base of the wall begins only a few dozen yards beyond it. Either end of the cliff can be scrambled around to reach the top.

ar_dam_boulders.blurb: A cluster of sandstone boulders near the dam at Lake Lincoln, set apart from the roped crags on the lake's north shore. The problems here suit moderate climbers well: most fall between V0 and V4, with a few harder lines stretching toward V7. Block Crack, Block Left and Block Party are good places to start, and PJ and Hangover are well-liked at V3. Bring a pad and expect some walking through the woods between boulders, since a few of the approaches take a little route-finding. It makes an easy add-on to a day at the main wall.

ar_dardanelle_rock.blurb: A small sport crag of hard, angular sandstone right in the town of Dardanelle, beside the Arkansas River. The rock is harder and more angular than the sandstone found farther north in the state, and holds often feel like they face the wrong direction, which makes the movement distinctive. Most routes are bolted and many have fixed draws, with grades concentrated in the 5.10 to 5.12 range and only a few easier lines such as Easy Tiger. Rebel Yell, Chick Magnet and Moneyshot are among the standouts. The wall is next to a road, so the walk in is very short.
ar_dardanelle_rock.parking_note: Take Highway 7 south through Russellville and across the river into Dardanelle, then follow 2nd Street to Dam Road. A pull-off across from the road sign serves the crag.
ar_dardanelle_rock.approach: Under five minutes on foot to nearly every line.

ar_main_wall_2.blurb: The most visible section of the Area 74 boulders in the Ozarks, a roadside sandstone wall with pockets, crimps and slopers. All of the climbing here is bouldering, and it leans hard: most problems fall between V4 and V6, with a good number higher still, so it suits strong climbers more than newcomers. Styles range from short, powerful moves to tall highballs. Paved paths lead to many of the problems, and steps climb up into the wooded areas behind. The Fin, Hood Rich and Squeeze Play are the names to know. Bring plenty of pads for the taller lines.

ar_dead_dog_energamata_walls.blurb: A pair of walls on the East Main Bluff at Sam's Throne, in the Boston Mountains near Mount Judea. The sandstone is solid and well featured, and many lines cross a roof partway up before finishing on featured vertical faces. Sport routes outnumber trad here, and the grades sit mostly in the 5.10 to 5.12 range. Dead Dog, Inherit the Wind and Doggy Style are the sport favorites, while Energemata offers an easier trad option. Fall is a pleasant time to visit, when the surrounding hardwoods are in color.
ar_dead_dog_energamata_walls.parking_note: Head south from Mount Judea on Highway 123; after four or five miles a wooden sign on the right marks the area.

ar_valley_of_the_blind.blurb: An exposed valley of sandstone a short drive south of Sam's Throne, home to some of the longest and most dramatic lines in the area and among the taller bolted cliffs in Arkansas. Sport routes slightly outnumber trad, and the grades run steep: most of the climbing sits between 5.10 and 5.12, with very little below that. Painted Warrior, The Black and Shadow Line are the hard headliners, while Wisdom and Folly and Silent Power give a way into the 5.11 range. Expect a downhill hike to the walls, and plan for a longer day than at nearby crags.
ar_valley_of_the_blind.parking_note: Drive about a mile south of Sam's Throne along the same road and pull off at the near end of the guardrail on the west side.
ar_valley_of_the_blind.approach: A trail leaves the tree line near a yellow sign, bears right at a seasonal waterfall, and drops downhill to the walls in roughly ten minutes.

ar_far_east_the.blurb: One of the most popular sectors at Horseshoe Canyon Ranch, a steep sandstone area on the east side of the property near Jasper. Most of the routes are bolted, with some trad lines mixed in, and the grades range from the 5.8 range up to 5.12, centered on 5.10 and 5.11. It earns a reputation for being fun at every level. Orange Crush, Gracie's Eight and First Time Up give moderate climbers good options, while Supersoul Sureshot and Purple Nehi challenge harder leaders. The hike here is the longest of any sector on the ranch.
ar_far_east_the.parking_note: Leave the car at the ranch lot near the Trading Post, which is on the south side of Highway 74 about seven miles west of Jasper.
ar_far_east_the.approach: Roughly 15 minutes on foot, the longest hike at the ranch. Head toward the Cliffs of Insanity and move right when you reach the wall.

ar_natural_disaster_area.blurb: One of the two largest sections of Jamestown Crag, a sandstone bluff line near Batesville in northeast Arkansas. Most of the routes here are bolted, with a few trad lines, and the grades cover a wide range from the low 5.x numbers through 5.12, with the most climbs between 5.8 and 5.11. The crag has a primitive, undeveloped feel with forested surroundings. Don't Stretch It and White Lightening are the popular lines. Expect slippery footing on the bluff descents after rain, and a rough, muddy road in.
ar_natural_disaster_area.parking_note: From Highway 167 south of Batesville, take Highway 230 west and turn onto Jamestown Loop. The final stretch is rough gravel that turns muddy in wet weather; park in the lot at its end.

ar_valley_of_the_blind_climbs.blurb: The bolted and trad lines at Valley of the Blind, an exposed sandstone valley near Sam's Throne. Sport routes outnumber trad, and the grades are steep, with the bulk between 5.10 and 5.12 and only a handful easier. Painted Warrior, The Black and Wet Warrior are the hard sport climbs, Wisdom and Folly and Silent Power are strong 5.11 options, and Cosmic Hippo is the trad pick. These are among the longest and most dramatic lines in the region, so plan for a full day and a downhill hike to reach the base.
ar_valley_of_the_blind_climbs.parking_note: Drive about a mile south of Sam's Throne along the same road and pull off at the near end of the guardrail on the west side.
ar_valley_of_the_blind_climbs.approach: A trail leaves the tree line near a yellow sign, bears right at a seasonal waterfall, and drops downhill to the walls in roughly ten minutes.

ar_amateur_route_area.blurb: A friendly section of Jamestown Crag, a sandstone bluff near Batesville in northeast Arkansas, sitting directly below where the trail meets the cliff line. Nearly all the climbing is bolted, with a few trad and top-rope options, and the grades run from about 5.5 to 5.12, with plenty of moderates between 5.7 and 5.10 and a couple of excellent harder lines such as Delusions of Grandeur and Wet Dreams. Pee Green, Hot For Teacher and Pagan on Sunday are good warm-ups. The setting is forested and primitive, and the road in turns muddy when it rains.
ar_amateur_route_area.parking_note: From Highway 167 south of Batesville, take Highway 230 west and turn onto Jamestown Loop. The final stretch is rough gravel that turns muddy in wet weather; park in the lot at its end.
